newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: French embassy car attacked in Belgrade scuffle.
newsitem.headline: French embassy car attacked in Belgrade scuffle.

text.p: A French diplomatic car was attacked and the driver punched, kicked and his head driven against the windscreen by young men in Belgrade on Tuesday, witnesses and local radio said.
Shots were fired during the scuffle, and according to an independent radio station, this saved the unidentified driver from being lynched by the youths.
"The car which was attacked belonged to the French embassy, and if the man who fired his gun in the air had not done so, the car's driver would very likely have been lynched," Index radio reported.
The incident, which occurred after dark, followed an afternoon rally by 80,000 opposition supporters in the same downtown spot: Republic Square.
The night duty officer at the French embassy told Reuters the silver Audi 100 with black registration plates was an embassy car. He said he did not know who was driving it.

A Reuter photographer recognised one of the men, wearing a baseball cap and with a whistle in his mouth, as having been in the crowd that had gathered earlier to demand the reinstatement of local election results last November.

"Dozens of youngsters were drinking brandy in front of the police," said one witness. "Later, when the police had left, they threw stones and pretended to be traffic police. When one car refused to stop, the hooligans broke its rear window. They were clearly drunk."
The photographer said the youths were telling motorists to sound their horns, but the driver of the embassy car appeared not to understand, suggesting he might have been a foreigner.
Someone, possibly a plainclothes policeman, fired shots in the air with his pistol, the witnesses said.
They said police arrived at the scene and arrested two youths.
For 77 days, opposition coalition supporters and students have held largely peaceful demonstrations in Belgrade demanding that Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic agree democratic reforms.
